hints: Read values from left to right; the first value cannot need adjustment.
For each later value, it must be at least the adjusted previous value.
If it is too small, raise it to that previous value and add the difference to the move count.
analogy: A rising staircase can be built by lifting each step only as high as the step before it.
example: For 3,2,5,1,7, the adjusted sequence is 3,3,5,5,7; lifts are 1 and 4, totaling 5.
algorithm: Keep the previous adjusted value. For each x, add max(0, previous-x) to the answer and set previous to max(previous,x).
correctness: Any valid nondecreasing result must make each position at least the already-required previous value; choosing exactly that minimum never adds unnecessary moves.
complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
